correctness.rationale: For every integer m,k>=2, the complete all-vertex zero-sum distance-power quadratic form is an explicit global P-block plus branch R-blocks and leaf residuals. The exact identity P=R+mH and a strict two-function Laplace Gram representation imply H negative definite on (1,2), so P PSD implies every other sector PD. At p=1, P is PD; before p=log2(2m/(m-1)) it becomes singular. A root with P11>0 is PSD and the strict-inheritance theorem rules out any second such root. Rank-one perturbation in k and strictly negative-definite perturbation in m give strict threshold decreases. Simple-eigenvalue perturbation yields the stated sharp asymptotics. The standalone script rebuilt all-vertex path distances and passed 1,257 deterministic assertions; its finite checks are corroboration, not the proof.

value.rationale: Natural finite spherically symmetric rooted trees with two independent branching parameters supply the first nonlinear family beyond elementary stars. Prior primary research numerically calculated even the binary height-two exponent and explicitly identified precise finite-tree values as difficult. The new claim is a complete infinite-family exact sharpness theorem, with the uniquely obstructing symmetry sector, two strictly monotone parameter laws and two sharp independent asymptotic coefficients. These relations are not merely routine parameter substitution or arbitrary narrow finite computations.
